title: Super Moist Chocolate Cupcakes
description: Rich, fudgy, easy chocolate cupcakes made from simple everyday ingredients. Over-the-top with chocolate buttercream.
equipment: 12-count muffin pan plus a second pan
icing knife or piping bag with a Wilton 1M tip

items.note: optional; instant coffee powder also works

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (177°C). Line a 12-count muffin pan with cupcake liners, plus a couple of liners in a second pan; the batter makes a few extra.
In a large bowl, whisk the flour, cocoa, espresso powder, baking powder, baking soda and salt until thoroughly combined. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, both sugars, oil and vanilla until completely smooth.

Pour half the wet ingredients into the dry, then half the buttermilk, and whisk gently for a few seconds. Repeat with the rest of the wet ingredients and buttermilk. Stir until just combined; don't overmix. The batter will be thin.
Pour or spoon the batter into the liners, filling them only halfway so they don't overflow or sink. This matters.
Bake for 18 to 21 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Cool completely before frosting.
Frost with chocolate buttercream, swiped on with an icing knife or piped with a tip such as a Wilton 1M.

notes: Make ahead: bake the cupcakes 1 day in advance, keep them tightly covered at room temperature, and frost the day of serving. Unfrosted cupcakes freeze for up to 2 months; thaw overnight in the fridge and bring to room temperature before frosting.
Mini cupcakes: fill mini liners only halfway and bake for 10 to 12 minutes at 350°F (177°C).
Use natural cocoa powder, not Dutch-process.
Bring all refrigerated ingredients to room temperature so the batter mixes easily and evenly.
Buttermilk is required. To make a substitute, put 1 teaspoon of white vinegar or lemon juice in a liquid measuring cup, add whole milk to the ½-cup line, stir and let sit 5 minutes.
storage: Keep leftover cupcakes tightly covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
